tools.name: finding
tools.title: Record a finding
tools.description: Persist a conclusion you have personally reviewed about a specific file and line range. Supply `path` (any path in the active project, to select the database), `file` (project-relative path of the file), `line_start`/`line_end` (one-based inclusive), plus `severity`, `category`, `title`, and `description` (all your own judgment — SlugAudit never generates these). The finding is bound to the file's current content hash and `finding_read` reports it `stale` the moment that file changes. Findings last until this server exits. Use this to record reviewed issues, not raw diagnostics.

path.description: Any path inside the active project, used to select the database

file.description: Project-relative path of the file this finding is about

line_start.description: One-based inclusive start line of the finding

line_end.description: One-based inclusive end line of the finding

severity.description: Severity of the finding, e.g. critical/high/medium/low/informational

category.description: Category label for the finding, e.g. security/performance/correctness/style

title.description: Concise one-line title summarizing the finding (max 200 chars)

description.description: Detailed description of the finding, its impact, and any remediation (max 10000 chars)

tools.name: finding_read
tools.title: Read session findings
tools.description: Retrieve the findings recorded in this session (since this server started); a restart begins with none. Each carries `status`: `current` while its file still has the content hash it was written against, `stale` once that file changed or is gone. Supply `path` (any path in the active project) to select the project, and optionally `file` to filter to a specific file. Results are byte-cut pages under the shared `page`; call again with only `page.cursor` for the next page.

tools.name: leads
tools.title: Mechanical leads
tools.description: Want somewhere to start? Mechanical facts extracted from the index — call sites by callee name (unwrap, expect, panic, todo, unimplemented, assert), diagnostics, TODO/FIXME/HACK comment markers, and credential-shaped files. Nothing here is judged, ranked, scored, or ordered by importance: every item is a fact, and deciding which of them matter is entirely your call. Call with only `path` to get every mechanic with its row count, its distinct-file count (`files`) and `covers` (the languages that count read; a language missing there is unchecked, not absent), then call again with one `mechanic` id to get file/line rows, optionally narrowed with `pattern` (a path GLOB, e.g. `src/auth/*`; without `*`/`?` it is a substring match). Every response carries the shared `page` (`returned`, `total`, `complete`, `cursor`, `page_bytes`, `bytes_used`, `limited_by`, `revision_id`) plus the file denominators `files_total`/`files_covered`; there is no row cap, so a page is cut only by your `limit` (omit it for everything that fits) and by the page byte size (64 KiB by default; `page_bytes` raises it up to the server ceiling). To page, call again with only `page.cursor`: the pages are one stored answer from the first call, so edits made meanwhile never skip or repeat rows. For `mechanic`/`file`/`line` triples with no per-row text, pass `mode: compact`; with only `path` it then enumerates every mechanic in one response under the same completeness fields — the cheap way to see the whole surface. `notices` names any untested language the counts cover (only Rust is tested).

tools.name: mechanic
tools.title: Register auditor mechanics
tools.description: Register, remove, or list your own mechanics. The built-in `leads` mechanics are counting primitives, not a checklist: what counts as a signal in this codebase is your decision, and this is where you record it. `action: add` takes `id` (a-z, 0-9, _; never a built-in's or an existing entry's id), `language`, `query` (a Tree-sitter S-expression with exactly one capture; each distinct captured node is one row) and `note` (what it counts, in your words); a query that does not compile or whose trial scan ends `partial` is refused. It returns `first_count`: the `leads` response for that id (counts with `covers`, the first page of rows, `page`, `files_total`, `files_covered`, `files_not_parsed`). Entries are scoped to the project and live until this server exits or `project_control` `off` runs. `leads` and `report` list every entry with `source` (`session`, `builtin`) and its note, session first. `action: remove` deletes a registered entry by `id`; built-ins can never be removed or overridden. `action: list` returns every session and built-in mechanic, paged by cursor.

oneOf.description: Register `{id, language, query, note}` and return its first count.
Remove the registered entry `id`.
List every mechanic for this project.

path.description: Any path inside the active project. Required unless `cursor` is given.

action.description:
`add`, `remove`, or `list`. Required unless `cursor` is given; ignored
when `cursor` is given: a cursor only ever continues a stored `list`,
and never registers or removes anything.

cursor.description:
`list` only: the `page.cursor` of the previous page, copied exactly.
It continues the list as it was when the first page was read, without
a `path`; every other field except `page_bytes` is ignored. To page
the first count `add` returns, use that response's own `page.cursor`
with `leads`.

id.description:
`add`/`remove`: the entry id, 1-64 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `_`.
It can never be a built-in's id or one already registered.

language.description:
`add`: the grammar the query compiles against and the indexed files
it reads: exactly the lowercase name the index stores for a file
(`python`, `rust`, `javascript`, `tsx`), never a capitalised name or
a pack alias such as `shell` (use `bash`). Prose is refused.

query.description:
`add`: a Tree-sitter S-expression with exactly one capture, e.g.
`(call function: (identifier) @callee (#eq? @callee "eval"))`. Each
distinct captured node is one row. At most `max_structure_query_bytes`
bytes (16384 by default). A query that does not compile or whose trial
scan is incomplete is refused.

note.description:
`add`: what this entry counts, in your words (1-1024 bytes). It is
listed beside the entry in `leads`, `report` and `list`.

limit.description: `add`: maximum rows in the first page, as `leads`' `limit`.

page_bytes.description:
`add`: first page size in serialized JSON bytes, as `leads`'
`page_bytes`. `list`: the size of each page of listings.

tools.name: project_control
tools.title: Enable or disable a project
tools.description: Enable or disable SlugAudit for a project. Pass `action` = `"on"` to enable a project (creates the directory `.planning/slugaudit/`, which is the on switch, builds the database and runs the initial import), or `"off"` to disable it (deletes the whole `.planning/slugaudit/` directory, then `.planning` if it is empty). A project is on only while that directory exists; if its database is missing or broken, the next tool call rebuilds it. On `"on"` the runtime directory `.planning/slugaudit/` is also appended to the project-root `.gitignore` unless a rule that already ignores it is present; the response's `gitignore` field reports `added`, `already_ignored`, or `not_written` plus the file's path. `"off"` never edits `.gitignore`. Supply `path` to target a specific project root; defaults to the current directory. If the project was moved, copied, or re-extracted elsewhere (e.g. unzipped fresh from an archive), a stale `.planning/slugaudit/project.db` is discarded and rebuilt from source automatically — the agent does not need to delete it or re-enable manually. `profile` (`lean`, `audit` or `adaptive`) sets the resource profile for this session only; it is not saved.

tools.name: query
tools.title: Read-only SQL query
tools.description: Query the indexed codebase with read-only SQL. Key tables: files (id, path, language, byte_len, content — full text of every indexed file including non-code files), evidence (id, file_id, kind, start_line, end_line [1-based, inclusive], payload; kind is one of Structure, Import, Export, Comment, Docstring, Symbol, Diagnostic, Call), dependency_edges (from_file_id, to_file_id, raw_import_text, resolution_kind, confidence, syntax_unmodeled). To inspect code or file content directly from the DB without filesystem reads, query `files.content` (e.g. `SELECT content FROM files WHERE path = 'src/main.rs'`); `line_count(text)` and `line_range(text, start, end)` read a file by 1-based lines, and an oversized first row is clipped with a `substr` continuation in `clipped_cells`. To link evidence to file paths, always JOIN: `SELECT f.path, e.start_line FROM evidence e JOIN files f ON e.file_id = f.id WHERE e.kind = 'Symbol' AND json_extract(e.payload, '$.name') = 'configure'`. Schema discovery: `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'`. A statement SQLite cannot compile or run fails with code `sql_error`.

path.description: Any path inside the active project. Required unless `cursor` is given.

sql.description:
Read-only SQL against the project's own database — arbitrary joins,
CTEs, and window functions are fine. Exactly one SELECT or WITH
statement is accepted. A PRAGMA is refused before anything is
prepared, wherever it sits in the input. The statement is then wrapped
as a subquery, which refuses every other kind (a write, EXPLAIN,
VACUUM, ATTACH, DDL). There is no keyword blocklist or table
allowlist. The schema-introspection table functions
(`pragma_table_info`, `pragma_table_xinfo`, `pragma_table_list`,
`pragma_index_list`, `pragma_index_info`, `pragma_index_xinfo`,
`pragma_foreign_key_list`) are ordinary SELECTs and work.
Required unless `cursor` is given; ignored with a `cursor`.

cursor.description:
The previous page's `page.cursor`, copied exactly. It continues the
stored result of the call that returned it, so `path` and `sql` are
not needed (and are ignored). Omit it to run a new query.

Page size in serialized JSON bytes. Omit it for the server default
(64 KiB unless configured otherwise; the response's `page.page_bytes`
says what applied). A larger value returns a larger page, up to the
hard ceiling `max_query_response_bytes`. Pages are cut on a row
boundary; when the first row alone is larger than the page, its
TEXT/BLOB cells are clipped to fit and listed in `clipped_cells` with
the `substr` expression that continues each one. May change between
pages.

tools.name: report
tools.title: Project snapshot
tools.description: Automatic project snapshot: file/language counts, parser failures, evidence-kind counts, open findings, and inbound/outbound dependency-edge counts. Use this first to understand the project's shape, then query for specifics. No score, no risk leads. `notices` flags untested languages (only Rust is tested); `languages[].tested` says which.

path.description: Any path inside the active project: its root, or a file/directory under it.

DatabaseDiscard.description:
Caller-facing record reported on the single call that discarded and rebuilt
a corrupt or stale `project.db`.

CompletenessEnvelope.description: Counts that say whether the rest of the response is the whole truth.

file_kind_counts.description:
Every `files` row by `file_kind`. `indexed` is the set with content and
metadata — its structural evidence may still be missing, which
`indexed_files_without_evidence` counts; `binary` was sampled and
deliberately not parsed; `skipped` was discovered but never read, so
it has no content.

file_class_counts.description:
Every `files` row by `file_class` — where the code came from, derived
from the path alone (`sync::classify`): `authored` (the project's own
source), `generated` (a machine-written file: a `generated` path token
or a codegen suffix such as `.pb.go` / `.g.dart` / `.min.js`), or
`vendored` (a third-party tree: `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, …). A
mechanic whose rows are dominated by one class can be summarised in a
sentence instead of paged row by row. `vendored` subsumes `generated`
when a path matches both. A path heuristic, not a verdict: it says
where a file came from, never whether it matters.

skipped_file_count.description:
`files` rows with `file_kind = 'skipped'`, i.e. files that exist in the
project but are not in the index.

skipped_by_reason.description:
Those skipped rows grouped by `skip_reason`. This is the "why" paired
with `index_partial`. A file with no representable `files.path` (a
non-UTF-8 name) cannot appear here; it is counted by
`unrepresentable_path_count` instead.

extraction_completeness_counts.description:
Every `files` row by `extraction_completeness`, so "text present but
not parsed" (`ContentOnly`) is visible as itself instead of vanishing
into a parser-failure count.

index_partial.description:
True when the index does not cover every file discovery found in the
current tree: an existence row is `skipped`, or a discovered file's
path has no UTF-8 representation and therefore no `files` row at all.
False means every discovered file is represented by a row here.

unrepresentable_path_count.description:
Discovered files whose project-relative path is not valid UTF-8, so
no `files` row can represent them and they cannot be stored, skipped
or named in this report. Sync persists this set during every full
discovery, so the count is read from the index rather than from a
walk run for this report. It is project-level — describing the tree
as of the sync that produced this report, not a particular revision —
and is included in `index_partial`.

evidence_capped_file_count.description:
Files whose stored evidence was cut short by an evidence cap: each
carries the `evidence:truncated` diagnostic appended by
`sync::sample::apply_evidence_limits`. Their structural record is
incomplete in a way this report cannot recover, so an agent counting
`evidence_counts` for them is counting a floor, not a total.

indexed_files_without_evidence.description:
`indexed` rows with no evidence at all — content is present and
readable, but the index holds nothing structural about them (a
language with no loaded parser, or a file that parsed to nothing).
Binary and skipped rows are excluded: no evidence is their expected
state, not a gap.

prose_files_not_parsed.description:
`indexed` files stored as `language = 'prose'` (Markdown,
reStructuredText, AsciiDoc, Org, plain text): content is stored and
searchable, but no grammar is run on them by design, so they are
`ContentOnly`, have no evidence, and are counted in
`indexed_files_without_evidence`, yet they are not parser failures and
never appear in `parser_failure_*`. Subtract this from those counts to
see the files that lack evidence for another reason.

oversize_for_parse_file_count.description:
`indexed` files larger than `max_parse_bytes` (`parse_error_reason =
'oversize_for_parse'`): content is stored and searchable via `query`,
but no grammar was run, so they have no evidence and every `leads`
mechanic that reads evidence is blind to them. They are also listed
among the parser failures and counted in `leads.files_not_parsed`.

parse_timeout_file_count.description:
`indexed` files a parse of which was cut at the sync deadline
(`parse_error_reason = 'parse_timeout'`): content is stored; no
evidence when the main parse was cut (`ContentOnly`), the main
parse's evidence but no call or binding evidence when a later
re-parse was (`Partial`). Also listed among the parser failures and
counted in `leads.files_not_parsed`.

SkipReasonCount.description: Row count for one recorded skip reason.

reason.description:
A short stable code from `files.skip_reason`: `oversize` (over the
per-file import ceiling), `not_utf8` (the bytes are not valid UTF-8),
`unreadable` (the read failed) or `stat_failed` (the stat failed, so
`files.byte_len` is NULL: size unknown, not 0). Every skipped row
carries one; a skipped row without a reason fails the report.

count.description: Number of skipped `files` rows with this `reason`.

CompletenessCount.description: Row count for one extraction-completeness value.

extraction_completeness.description:
One of `Full`, `Partial`, `ContentOnly`, `Unavailable`. `ContentOnly`
means the file's text is in `files.content` but no parser ran over it
— the file is readable even though it has no structural evidence.
`Unavailable` means no content is retained at all (binary, or skipped).

count.description: Number of `files` rows with this `extraction_completeness` value.

LanguageCount.description:
How many discovered files the last revision attributed to one detected
language.

tested.description:
Whether this project's tests cover the language (only Rust). An
untested language is parsed best-effort and has a line in `notices`.

EvidenceKindCount.description: How many evidence rows the current revision holds for one kind.

ParserFailureFile.description:
A file whose parse failed or was not attempted, with the recorded
outcome, reason, completeness and parser availability.

parse_error_reason.description:
Why no tree was extracted: the grammar's load error, the parser's
hard error (not just syntax error nodes), or a stable code —
`oversize_for_parse` (content over `max_parse_bytes`, never parsed) or
`parse_timeout` (the parse was cancelled at the deadline). `None` when
no grammar exists for the file or for `SyntaxErrors`.

extraction_completeness.description:
One of `Full`, `Partial`, `ContentOnly`, `Unavailable`. `ContentOnly`
means the file's text *is* indexed but no parser ran over it — the
row is listed for availability reasons, not because extraction
failed, and its content can still be read from `files.content`.

parser_availability.description:
One of `Available`, `Unavailable`, `LoadFailed`. Separates
`ContentOnly` rows that have no parser for their language
(`Unavailable`) from ones whose parser could not be loaded
(`LoadFailed`), which a completeness value alone cannot.

ImportResolutionCount.description:
How many import edges fell into each resolution bucket. `Resolved` edges
land on a project file; `External` and `Unresolved` edges carry no target.

DependencyEdgeTotals.description: Edge totals in both directions, over the whole revision.

outbound_edge_count.description:
`count(*) FROM dependency_edges`: every edge, since every edge
originates at a file (`from_file_id` is `NOT NULL`).

inbound_edge_count.description:
Edges whose `to_file_id` names a row in `files` — the subset that
lands on a project file. `Unresolved` and `External` edges carry no
target, and `import_resolution` splits those two apart; this total
groups them only by their absence of a target.

outbound_file_count.description: Distinct files that are the source of at least one edge.

inbound_file_count.description: Distinct files that are the target of at least one edge.

ReportMechanics.description: The mechanics section of a report.

note.description: Present on the first `report` for this project on this server only; `null` after.

entries.description: Every loaded mechanic for this project: session, then builtin.

note.description: The author's note; `null` for a built-in.

language.description: The grammar a registered entry runs on; `null` for a built-in.

query.description: A registered entry's Tree-sitter query; `null` for a built-in.

MechanicSource.description: Where a mechanic comes from. Listings are ordered session, then builtin.

oneOf.description: Registered with `mechanic add` on this server; ends when it exits.
Shipped with SlugAudit; can never be removed or overridden.

revision_id.description: Revision id of the index this snapshot was read from.

database_discard.description:
Present only when this call discarded and rebuilt the project
database (corruption, version bump, root mismatch), and why. Session
findings live in their own database and are not affected.

file_count.description:
Rows in `files`: every discovered file whose project-relative path is
representable as UTF-8, whether or not it was indexed. A discovered
path that is not valid UTF-8 cannot have a row and is counted by
`completeness.unrepresentable_path_count` instead. Read
`completeness.file_kind_counts` to see how many of these rows have
content (`indexed`), are binary, or were skipped — this number alone
does not mean "files with evidence".

completeness.description:
Whether every count above is the whole truth: rows by kind, skipped
rows by reason, rows by extraction completeness, and a partial-index
flag. See [`CompletenessEnvelope`].

languages.description:
Detected language of each `files` row, with its file count; grouped by
language and ordered by language name. Rows with no detected language
are not listed.

notices.description:
One line per untested code language in `languages` (prose is not one):
its grammar is downloaded on first use and only Rust is tested, so its
results are best-effort. Empty when there is nothing to say.

evidence_counts.description: Evidence rows by `kind` across the current revision, ordered by kind.

parser_failure_count.description:
Uncapped total of files whose parser was unavailable or whose parse
failed — the same predicate `parser_failure_files` lists. Larger than
the returned list's length means the list was truncated at
`MAX_PARSER_FAILURE_FILES`; equal means the list is complete.

parser_failure_files.description:
Up to `MAX_PARSER_FAILURE_FILES` files with parse failures, ordered
by path.

open_finding_count.description:
This session's findings that are `current`: findings whose file
content hash still matches the hash they were written against.
Findings invalidated by a later content change are `stale` and are not
counted.

import_resolution.description: How many import edges are Resolved, Unresolved and External.

dependency_edges.description:
The same graph counted in both directions: how many edges leave a
file, how many land on one, and how many files are on each end.
Pure arithmetic over `dependency_edges`. Per-file counts and traversal
are the `blast_radius_outbound.sql`, `blast_radius_inbound.sql` and
`blast_radius_closure.sql` recipes under `slugaudit://queries/`.

diagnostic_count.description:
Total number of Diagnostic evidence items (e.g. linter or compiler
diagnostics extracted from source files).

unsupported_language_unresolved_count.description:
Of the `Unresolved` count in `import_resolution`, how many come from
import syntax the resolver couldn't parse at all — `extract_reference`
returned `None` on the raw text (e.g. Go's `import "fmt"`), as
opposed to an import whose syntax was parsed but matched no project
file (e.g. a stdlib module like `kotlin.math.max`). Both are stored as
`Unresolved` edges; this count is the first kind
(`dependency_edges.syntax_unmodeled = 1`).

credential_pattern_file_count.description:
How many rows in `files` match common credential-file patterns
(`.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, etc. — the same list the
SQL below matches, and the same list `leads`' `credential_files`
rows use). These paths are recorded like any other file, including
when the file was skipped and no content was retained. The count is
a path match, not a statement about the file's content.

mechanics.description:
Every mechanic `leads` counts — session entries for this project, then
the built-ins — with its source and the author's note. On the first
`report` for this project on this server only, `note` also explains how
mechanics work.

its end with `cursor`, then make a new request with `start_after_file`
= `next_start_after_file`.

`structure` or custom-mechanic scan: the execution time budget stopped
the scan before every file finished. Read the stored result with
`cursor`, then resume after `resume_after_file` (or `next_start_after_file`).

`structure` or custom-mechanic scan: Tree-sitter's per-file `QueryCursor`
match-state limit (`65,536` states) was exceeded on a file, so some
matches were dropped (`completeness` is `partial`). Narrow the Tree-sitter
pattern so no match states overflow.

`structure` only: one or more matching files exceeded `max_parse_bytes`
(`files_over_parse_limit` > 0) or produced no syntax tree
(`unparsed_files` non-empty).

DatabaseDiscard.description:
Caller-facing record reported on the single call that discarded and rebuilt
a corrupt or stale `project.db`.

StructureMatch.description:
One capture match mapped back to source coordinates, with the
clipping/extraction flags that bound its `text`.

start_line.description: One-based, inclusive line where the match starts.

end_line.description: One-based, inclusive line where the match ends.

text_truncated.description: True when `text` was truncated to fit the text/snippet cap or spans multiple lines in snippet mode.

extraction_failed.description: True when UTF-8 decoding or capture naming failed.

page.description:
Paging for `matches`. `cursor` pages through the stored result;
`completeness` says whether the scan behind it covered everything.

language.description: The grammar this query ran against.

notices.description: One line when `language` is untested; empty otherwise.

matches.description: This page's matches in scan order.

files_not_scanned.description: Multi-file only: matching files past the memory window not loaded in this call.

bytes_not_scanned.description: Content bytes of those unscanned files.

next_start_after_file.description: The `start_after_file` for the new request that scans past this partial result.

unparsed_files.description: Multi-file only: files the parser produced no syntax tree for.

files_over_parse_limit.description: Multi-file only: matching files larger than `max_parse_bytes` (or the scan window).

parse_timed_out_file.description: Multi-file only: set when the execution time budget ran out while this file was parsed.
